course_name_original: Redes de Sensores: Aplicaciones Médicas e IoT
course_name_en: Sensor Networks: Medical and IoT Applications

learning_outcomes.text: To know the different communication networks and sensor networks (Internet of Things, IoT) for data collection and transport, mainly those oriented to M2M (machine-to-machine communications).
To know the basic parameters of communication networks: coverage, bandwidth, transmission techniques, application scenarios.
To know how to characterize transmission mechanisms and phenomena affecting transmission (distortion, noise), as well as techniques to minimize them (encodings, MIMO).

To know how to choose the most appropriate data acquisition and transport system for a given application, based on parameters such as coverage area, application scenario, amount of data to be collected and transmitted, real-time requirements.
Ability to discuss the advantages and limitations of communication and sensor network technologies.
To know the different types of sensors and their applications. Emphasis on medical applications (e-Medicine and e-Health), Smart applications (e.g., Smart-cities), and applications for Industry 4.0.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to wireless networks. Wireless transmission mechanisms and phenomena affecting them (noise, multipath). Access schemes, modulation, encoding.
Communication networks for data transport. M2M networks in 4G and 5G. Internet of Things (IoT). Specifications (coverage, frequency bands, bandwidth, access and encoding techniques), scope and reach.
Types of sensors and information acquisition elements.
Applications of sensor networks and IoT for data collection and transport.
Applications for Industry 4.0, Smart applications (Smart-Cities and Environmental Management, Smart Buildings), logistics and transport, e-medicine and e-health, open information sources.

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (T1) - Description, project requirements and preliminary design
Practical work (T1) - Development of a sensor subsystem
Practical work (T1) - Development of a monitoring subsystem
Practical work (T1) - Integration and verification of the final system
Practical work (T1) - Intermediate presentation and final demo

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the practical work (T1) during the course is evaluated based on several components: description, project requirements, preliminary design, detailed design, development of a sensor subsystem, development of a monitoring subsystem, integration and verification of the final system, intermediate presentation, and final demo (totaling 9 points). The final exam accounts for 1 point. In the extraordinary call, there will be a theoretical exam (maximum 5 points) covering all theoretical content, and a practical work evaluated by an oral defense (maximum 5 points). Differentiated evaluation follows the same guidelines as the extraordinary call.
